acceptance_predicates.description: Setup, plan creation, validation, run, sweep, report, compare, and TUI flows let users select agents, providers, models, tools, and workloads by stable display names only.

Each selected name resolves through one catalog/config resolver to the canonical executable, provider endpoint, model identifier, workload definition, version, and integrity metadata without requiring the user to enter or copy those values.

The resolver rejects ambiguous, stale, missing, or name-to-artifact mismatches with a clear name-based remediation; plan/run binding uses the resolved identity rather than trusting a separately supplied path or hash.

Default human prompts, status, errors, and reports expose names and actionable choices, not filesystem paths, hashes, opaque versions, or internal identity fields; JSON retains machine-readable resolved metadata only where required by its contract.
The standalone asb-tui and embedded TUI consume the same name catalog and resolver, with identical choices and no duplicated path/hash/version entry workflow.

definition_of_done: After AR-1832, a fresh user can complete the supported ASB workflow by choosing names, while ASB internally resolves and verifies all physical and versioned identities consistently across CLI and TUI.

inputs.description: AR-1832 qualified setup-output and explicit config-bound benchmark route.
Configured and discovered catalogs for agents, providers, models, tools, and workloads.
ASB CLI/TUI and standalone asb-tui selection and handoff contracts.

outputs.description: Shared name-to-identity resolver and persisted logical selections.
Name-only human setup, execution, and analysis flows with paired CLI/TUI coverage.
Contract and journey evidence proving mismatch prevention and name-first operation.

gates.description: Focused tests prove every supported logical name resolves deterministically and ambiguous or mismatched identities fail with name-based remediation.
A clean-project CLI and paired TUI journey completes setup, selection, benchmark, and analysis without user-supplied paths, hashes, or versions.
Existing explicit-config, safety, privacy, and development-channel contracts remain green.
